metadata.title: beam_mu performance: per-row analytic intervals, bit-identical output (#289)
guardrails: follow [[iec-61217-dicom-patient-position-beam-projection]]: geometry and signs are not touched; only work is pruned
follow [[relative-tolerance-check-passes-everything-when-expected-overflows]]: no tolerance comparisons; bit-identity is np.array_equal
follow [[simpleitk-array-view-of-temporary-image-reads-freed-memory]]: no array views of SimpleITK images (memory cut is deferred)
commit gate: at most 5 files per commit; naming private functions in docs/commits needs CLAUDE_ALLOW_PRIVATE_API=1 with the list in the commit body
beam_volume.py: no try/except, no quiet_call, only raise CaseRefused(REASON_BEAM_VOLUME) (test_beam_volume_catches_and_quiets_nothing)

tasks.title: Frozen reference oracle and bit-identity test matrix
tasks.test_approach: tests/beam_mu_reference.py is a verbatim copy of today's (324e2b2) _axis, _add and the chunk loop of beam_mu from src/rt_dataprep/beam_volume.py, exposed as reference_beam_mu(points, ct) taking the output of beam_volume._points; the module itself imports nothing from rt_dataprep.beam_volume (pure numpy/SimpleITK). tests/test_beam_mu_oracle.py builds plans with the helpers in tests/test_beam_volume.py (ct_image, static, set_mlc, written, vmat_arc) and asserts np.array_equal(beam_volume.beam_mu(...), reference) over the spec's AC1 matrix (one factor at a time around a base case + a seeded random sample of >= 50 geometries), and the AC3 chunk test. These pass against today's code (the reference equals it); they are the guard for task-02. Default suite, keep total runtime under ~30 s. NOTE: these tests cannot go RED against today's code (the reference IS today's algorithm); that is expected, so write them green and commit. reference_beam_mu reads only the point-dict keys sad, weight, jaws, leaves, t, a; task-02 must keep those keys (extra keys allowed).
criteria: reference_beam_mu(points, ct) returns the (nz, ny, nx) float32 ndarray. Bit-identity everywhere means new = sitk.GetArrayFromImage(beam_mu(...)) has the same dtype and shape as the reference and new.tobytes() == ref.tobytes()
The AC1 base case and every one-factor variant use SAD 1000 on the default 61^3 / 5 mm ct_image(), except the explicit SAD 400, beyond-5000 mm and non-finite cases

The geometry-matrix, random-sample, degenerate-slope and mixed-plan tests in tests/test_beam_mu_oracle.py carry pytest.mark.filterwarnings('error::RuntimeWarning'); the non-finite cases do not (inf in _points' matmul warns in both paths) and run with warnings permitted
tests/beam_mu_reference.py contains the 324e2b2 _axis/_add/chunk-loop code verbatim (diff-able against git show 324e2b2:src/rt_dataprep/beam_volume.py) and does not import rt_dataprep.beam_volume

AC1: np.array_equal(beam_mu, reference) for each of: gantry {0,45,90,180,270,315}, collimator {0,30,90}, couch {0,90,270}, positions HFS/HFP/FFS/FFP, CT direction identity/ROT90/an oblique rotation, anisotropic spacing, off-centre isocenter, asymmetric jaws, MLC with closed/open/partly open pairs, jaw-only beam, MLC with no Y jaw, MLC with no X jaw, jaws on voxel centres (5 mm grid, multiples of 5) including gantry 90 and 270, SAD 400 and SAD 1000

AC1: a seeded random sample of at least 50 geometries is bit-identical, with ranges pinned so every case is interval-path by construction on the default 61^3 grid: SAD in [800, 1200], spacing <= 5 mm, |isocenter offset| <= 50 mm per axis, random gantry/collimator/couch angles, jaws and leaf openings

AC1: rows from plan_rows are copied and mutated, one case each: jaw_x1=nan, jaw_y2=inf, one mlc_positions entry nan, the last leaf_position_boundaries entry inf, isocenter_x=inf; plus a CT grid origin beyond 5000 mm in beam coordinates. Each case either raises CaseRefused(REASON_BEAM_VOLUME) in beam_mu exactly where the reference path (beam_volume._points + reference) would, or is bit-identical to the reference
AC3: with CHUNK_VOXELS monkeypatched to force at least 3 z-chunks, output is bit-identical to the single-chunk output and to the reference

AC1: a 3-beam plan with overlapping fields, beam 2 at SAD 400 gantry 45 (falls back under Design 3) between beams 1 and 3 at SAD 1000, and the same plan with the beam order reversed, are bit-identical to the reference
The full default suite passes

tasks.title: beam_volume: per-row interval engine with interior credit, exact edge band and full-loop fallback
tasks.test_approach: Red first: add AC2 tests to tests/test_beam_mu_oracle.py that spy on beam_volume._add (the fallback, today's code) and assert zero fallback calls on SAD 1000 cases, and that FALLBACK_DEPTH_FRACTION set to 0 and to 1e9 both give output bit-identical to the reference on the same SAD 1000 case; these fail until the engine exists. Then implement spec Design 1-6 in beam_volume.py. The task-01 oracle matrix must stay green throughout; any mismatch is fixed by a larger pad or stricter fallback, never a tolerance.
criteria: Spec Design 1: per row, interior voxels (clear every inequality by > EDGE_MARGIN_MM tightened, minus a 1-voxel pad) get the weight via a contiguous float32 add without the per-voxel test; edge-band voxels (inside the epsilon-relaxed, 1-voxel-padded, grid-clipped, deduplicated union) run today's full jaw + searchsorted test once; others get nothing; each voxel gets at most one add per point in point order

Spec Design 2: relaxed inequalities are evaluated at both row ends; no slope threshold, no division by a slope smaller than 2*eps/(N-1), and no RuntimeWarning is emitted in the oracle tests (run with -W error::RuntimeWarning)

Spec Design 3: a point falls back to _add over the full chunked grid when any grid corner has depth < FALLBACK_DEPTH_FRACTION*SAD (0.5), when any of t, a, jaws, leaf positions or leaf boundaries is non-finite, or when any grid corner's beam coordinate exceeds MAX_COORD_MM (5000); fallback is a geometric check with no try/except
Spec Design 4: jaw values stay Python floats and leaf arrays stay float64 as aperture() builds them; the per-voxel test and the float32 adds are today's expressions unchanged
Spec Design 5: work is z-chunked by CHUNK_VOXELS, which stays monkeypatchable, and per-chunk interval arrays are bounded by the chunk

AC2: a beam_volume._add spy records zero calls across the whole random sample and every SAD 1000 one-factor AC1 case, and at least 1 call on each named fallback case (beyond-5000 mm origin, each non-finite case that is not refused, SAD 400 at gantry 45); FALLBACK_DEPTH_FRACTION=0 and =1e9 are both bit-identical to the reference on the same SAD 1000 case
All task-01 oracle tests (AC1, AC3) pass unchanged
AC5: the full existing suite passes, including test_beam_volume_catches_and_quiets_nothing; no existing test is edited
Public signatures beam_mu(plan, rows, ct, patient_position) and aperture(row) are unchanged; refusal checks run in the same order
_add (today's code) is called only for fallback points; the edge-band exact test is a separate function
On the 3-beam mixed plan the spy shows fallback and interval points processed interleaved in point order within each chunk
Before task-03 starts, the orchestrator runs AC14 once (-m slow -s) and records the measured ratio in findings.md
_points keeps the point-dict keys sad, weight, jaws, leaves, t, a (extra keys allowed) so reference_beam_mu keeps working

tasks.title: AC14 as a 10x speed-ratio gate against the frozen reference
tasks.test_approach: Rewrite test_ac14_full_size_vmat_case (still @pytest.mark.slow): run the new beam_mu first and record its wall time and peak RSS, then run tests/beam_mu_reference.py on the same _points output; assert np.array_equal and reference_wall / new_wall >= 10. Run it with `uv run --group dev pytest -m slow -s -k ac14` and record before/after wall time and RSS in findings.md.
criteria: AC4: test_ac14_full_size_vmat_case runs the new beam_mu first, prints its wall time and peak RSS before the reference runs, then asserts bit-identity with the reference and reference_wall / new_wall >= 10
RSS is printed and recorded in findings.md, not asserted
The slow test passes on this workstation and the measured ratio, both wall times and peak RSS are in findings.md
Any ratio < 10 is FAILED: task-03 never modifies src/, does not retry or tune, and /dev halts for the owner

AC14 also asserts the beam_volume._add spy recorded zero fallback calls, and findings.md records the new beam_mu wall time over 3 runs (min/median) against one reference run (the reference takes ~5.5 min)

deferred: Speedups beyond 10x: only if the real cohort run asks
